subject.title: Enhancement: Developer experience quick wins from code analysis

question: Should model-routed skill commands produce an opt-in trace diagnostic, be covered by the broader deterministic-injection direction, or remain documented without another signal?
rationale: The existing model-routed behavior is intentional and documented, so the permanent visibility level and its user-facing noise cannot be chosen safely without product intent.

options.title: Add opt-in trace signal
options.body: Emit a concise routing event through the existing session-scoped `/trace` surface without changing skill execution semantics or normal chat output.

options.title: Consolidate with injection work
options.body: Move the remaining context to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/52473 if maintainers intend deterministic injection to replace the model-routed behavior.

options.title: Keep documentation only
options.body: Treat the current slash-command documentation as sufficient and decline an additional operator-visible diagnostic.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in trace signal
recommendation.body: Emit a concise routing event through the existing session-scoped `/trace` surface without changing skill execution semantics or normal chat output.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the prior human product-context review and are connected to recent history around the affected skills and status surfaces.
